articleTitle: Optimization and Improvement of Tobacco Slice Machine Control System
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Innovations and Development of Information Technologies and Robotics (IDITR)
abstract: In order to solve the problems of tobacco block jamming and discontinuity after cutting when tobacco blocks with different rules and characteristics enter the tobacco block slicer. Optimize and improve the hardware and algorithm control logic of tobacco slice machine, Firstly, in the hardware improvement of the slicer equipment, the skew detection device of tobacco block, the height monitoring device of tobacco block and the position detection of half pack cutter are added; Secondly, in the optimization and improvement of algorithmic control logic, the tobacco block skew or irregular equipment early warning and tobacco block slicer cutting mode are added, that is, the whole tobacco block cutting mode and the half tobacco block cutting mode. Through the verification of the effect of the optimized and improved tobacco slicer, 100 batches of materials were verified to be produced. There were 35 times of skewed or irregular tobacco blocks after improvement, 35 times of early warning, 0 times of failure, and 0 times of discontinuity after cutting.

articleTitle: Research on Control Problems of vectored thruster AUVs with deep reinforcement learning
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Innovations and Development of Information Technologies and Robotics (IDITR)
abstract: In comparison to traditional fin and rudder propulsion devices, vector thruster autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) are renowned for their superior maneuverability, particularly at low or zero speeds. This study introduces a control strategy for vector thruster AUVs that employs deep reinforcement learning algorithms for three-dimensional random point and trajectory tracking. Simulation tests are conducted to investigate the motion of vector propelled AUVs. The utilization of deep reinforcement learning algorithms in this research demonstrates the potential of this approach in designing control strategies for vector thruster AUVs, ultimately enhancing maneuverability and autonomy in underwater exploration.

articleTitle: Derailment Detection of Mining Shaft's Rail Vehicle Using Machine Vision on Edge Device
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Innovations and Development of Information Technologies and Robotics (IDITR)
abstract: The railway system is pivotal in the mineral transportation industry. Due to rail track shape deformation or imbalance, the situation worsens. Stone, coal, and dust can also obstruct the mine rail transportation system. Moreover, derailment is very likely to happen, but conventionally, it is difficult to determine whether the vehicle is derailed. Scientists have developed different derailment detection techniques to overcome these difficulties, but most are implemented using sensors only. In challenging conditions, such as inside a mine shaft, sensor systems can fail for various reasons such as high dust levels, humidity, and fallen stones. These factors can easily destroy the sensors, especially if they are placed near to the ground surface. Machine vision, on the other hand, can detect objects from a greater distance than sensors. In our proposed system, we introduced a machine vision approach based on a Raspberry Pi, which combines YOLOv5n deep learning model and OpenCV to detect different types of derailment. Our system can be used as a rail track detection system by analyzing real-time video data.

articleTitle: Neural-Network-Based Inverse Dynamic Solutions of an Asymmetric Parallel Robot
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Innovations and Development of Information Technologies and Robotics (IDITR)
abstract: The dynamic models of parallel robots are more complicated due to the highly coupled kinematic chains compared with those of their counterparts-serial robot. The approximate dynamic models can be considered if the analytical solutions high cost in time due to the sophisticated calculations. To address this issue, this paper presents an alternative approach-the dynamic model based on the neural network. A three degrees-of-freedom parallel manipulator is introduced, followed by a detailed mathematical inverse dynamic model, which is replicated by three feedforward neural networks with various performance goals. A cascade forward neural network is also constructed to be compared with the feedforward neural network. The simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of these proposed neural networks.

articleTitle: The Application of Autoencoder In IMU Data Process
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Innovations and Development of Information Technologies and Robotics (IDITR)
abstract: Inertial Navigation System (INS) and Inertial Measurement Unit (IMU) are commonly used technologies in modern navigation and attitude control fields. INS is a navigation system based on the principle of inertial sensors, which calculates the position, velocity, and attitude of an object in real-time by measuring its acceleration and angular velocity and using initial attitude information. IMU is the core component of INS and usually contains three-axis accelerometers and three-axis gyroscopes. Accelerometers are used to measure linear acceleration, and gyroscopes are used to measure angular velocity. In INS and IMU, sensors usually collect the measurement values of multiple accelerometers and gyroscopes at high frequency. These measurement values contain a large amount of information, including object acceleration, angular velocity, and attitude changes. However, due to the large number of multi-axis sensors and high-frequency sampling, processing and analyzing these data may become complex and time-consuming. At this time, data dimensionality reduction techniques can be applied[1]. The main idea of this article is to add residual blocks to the traditional dimensionality reduction technique autoencoder to improve the model's ability to extract important features. This approach can transform high-dimensional sensor data into lower-dimensional representations while retaining essential motion features. This simplifies subsequent data processing, analysis, and storage processes, improves computing efficiency, and saves resources.

articleTitle: Digital Twinning Method Based on Multi-model Integration and Interoperation
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Innovations and Development of Information Technologies and Robotics (IDITR)
abstract: A digital twinning method for products based on multi-model integration and interoperation is proposed. Firstly, the definition and integration approach of multiple models are presented, and the specific connotations and creation methods of structural models, analytical models, and information models are elaborated. Secondly, a digital twin multi-model interoperation engine is designed, and the engine's interoperation mechanism of the engine is developed based on sequence relationships. Finally, the feasibility and effectiveness of this method are verified using an industrial robot as an example.

articleTitle: A Novel Seed Sorting Device Utilizing Vertical Centrifugation and Spectroscopy Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Innovations and Development of Information Technologies and Robotics (IDITR)
abstract: The ever-increasing demands for high-yield, superior crops have led to a heightened need for high-quality seeds, thus driving the robust development of the global seed sorting machine market. This paper designs a new type of seed sorting equipment that adopts advanced technologies such as near-infrared spectroscopy. By utilizing a vertical centrifugation device, the equipment achieves high-throughput seeding, not only improving the efficiency of single grain seed sorting but also significantly enhancing seed detection accuracy. This equipment offers an efficient solution that is expected to provide a reference for high-throughput, high-precision seed sorting. Moreover, the versatility and high-performance of this device can aid in achieving long-term goals of increasing crop yields and reducing waste, thereby addressing the problem of high initial investment costs.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Leveling and Balancing Algorithm for 6x6 Electric Unmanned Ground Vehicle with Active Hydro-Pneumatic Suspension System
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Innovations and Development of Information Technologies and Robotics (IDITR)
abstract: This study centers on developing a leveling and balancing algorithm for a 6x6 electric unmanned ground vehicle (UGV) featuring an active hydro-pneumatic suspension system. UGVs have garnered considerable attention for their adaptability across diverse domains, making stability and levelness crucial for their success in challenging terrains. The research unveils an advanced algorithm for the active hydro- pneumatic suspension system, founded on a deep comprehension of UGV dynamics and environmental interactions. This algorithm computes the requisite arm system angles based on user inputs, ensuring the UGV adapts to shifting terrain conditions while preserving balance and stability. It continuously checks arm angles and pressure limits to guarantee safe operation. This study carries significance in its potential to heighten the overall performance and safety of autonomous ground vehicles. Leveraging active hydro-pneumatic suspension technology, the algorithm facilitates stable UGV operation. It enables the UGV to position and utilize attached equipment with stability, enhancing mission efficiency by executing elevation- depression and angular movements. UGVs can now effectively conduct tasks in challenging terrains, as demonstrated through successful real and Webots platform experiments. The algorithm has been seen to effectively balance and level the UGV based on user inputs and road characteristics. In conclusion, this study presents the design and implementation of a novel leveling and balancing algorithm for a 6x6 electric unmanned ground vehicle equipped with an active hydro-pneumatic suspension system.

articleTitle: Design of Catheter Drive Mechanism for Vascular Interventional Surgery Robot
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Innovations and Development of Information Technologies and Robotics (IDITR)
abstract: Aiming at the advantages of interventional surgical robot system in flexibility, safety and accuracy, a compact continuous delivery catheter drive mechanism for interventional surgical robot is designed and its structure is optimized and analyzed. Firstly, the structure analysis of the axial feed part and the circumferential rotation part of the catheter drive mechanism is carried out to ensure the flexibility and accuracy of the mechanism. Secondly, a solution to the problem of difficult disinfection of the catheter drive mechanism is proposed, and its safety is improved by improving the structure. In addition, the catheter clamping mechanism has been improved to enhance the stability and handling performance of the mechanism. Finally, the kinematic performance of the mechanism is analyzed and evaluated in detail and verified by experiments.

articleTitle: Autonomous Underwater Vehicle Trajectory Tracking Based on Physics Informed Neural Network Modeling
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Innovations and Development of Information Technologies and Robotics (IDITR)
abstract: The autonomous underwater vehicle (AUV) serves as a foundational system for ocean exploration and understanding. Nonetheless, the intricate underwater environment and unpredictable dynamic disturbances can lead to decreased tracking accuracy. To address this challenge, this paper introduces a model predictive control (MPC) approach enhanced by Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs). This integration leverages PINNs to refine and predict the model within the traditional MPC framework, thereby enhancing the algorithm's robustness and dynamic responsiveness in the presence of external noise. Simulation results demonstrate the method's exceptional robustness and tracking accuracy in AUV trajectory tracking.

articleTitle: Research on Fabrication and Flight Performance of Minitype Robotic Butterfly with Visual Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Innovations and Development of Information Technologies and Robotics (IDITR)
abstract: Based on the aerodynamic principles of butterfly flight, the mechanical butterfly in small-scale is designed to investigate its biomimetic structure and flight performance in this paper. In order to achieve the collaboration mechanism among four wings, a novel flexible hinge is designed and developed. The robotic butterfly is manufactured with a maximum wingspan of 30 cm and a weight of 12 g, who can fly 5 m with a flight endurance of 3 min and a turning radius of 1.5 m. Equipped with a miniature monitoring camera, it could categorize the captured images during flight through picture processing and machine learning techniques based on support vector. This robotic butterfly is expected to be applied in tasks such as aerial monitoring, earthquake relief, and complex terrain surveying.<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>

articleTitle: Experimental Study on the Flow Field Characteristics of Vertical Venturi Valves
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Innovations and Development of Information Technologies and Robotics (IDITR)
abstract: A design proposal was put forward to enhance the precision of air flow control in the chemical laboratory, national biosynthesis laboratory, clean room, and other areas. This proposal involves the implementation of a vertical venturi air volume control valve. The flow field distribution characteristics of this valve were analyzed using Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) technology. CFD technology was utilized to model and simulate the flow field of the vertical venturi air volume control valve. Subsequently, the optimization design for enhancing the adjustment accuracy of the vertical venturi air volume control valve was successfully accomplished. A performance test bench was constructed for the vertical venturi air volume control valve to facilitate the enhancement of product design. The test method and steps for measuring the air volume in the device were outlined, and the test results demonstrated that the designed vertical venturi air volume control valve met the specified accuracy requirements. Acquire expertise in the fundamental technology of these products and rapidly improve market competitiveness.

articleTitle: A Pose Reconstruction Model of Soft Robot Arms Based on Cosserat Theory
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Innovations and Development of Information Technologies and Robotics (IDITR)
abstract: Soft robots offer a wide range of useful applications in the fields of ground rescue, underwater grasping, space manipulation, and assistant maintenance. Pose information is important for controlling soft robotic arms; however, most pose reconstruction techniques are based on the constant curvature method. These methods are unreliable and oversimplification because they only focus on the stretching, bending, and twisting deformations of soft robotic arms. This work proposes a variable curvature pose reconstruction model based on the Cosserat theory, which involves stretching, bending, twisting, and shearing deformation to achieve accurate poses of soft robotic arms. With the help of a sensor network, it can rebuild the poses of soft robotic arms. The pose reconstruction error of the model is within 3%, according to simulation and testing data. This study offers a novel approach to soft robotic arms' pose reconstruction and improves the precision of the pose reconstruction.

articleTitle: A Loop Closing Network for Place Recognition and Loop Poses Estimation Tasks in LiDAR SLAM
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Innovations and Development of Information Technologies and Robotics (IDITR)
abstract: Loop closing plays a vital role in SLAM for robotic system, as it can be employed to mitigate accumulated drift. However, for 3D LiDAR SLAM, certain current approaches might struggle to accurately identify loops and often cannot rectify the complete 6-DoF loop poses, particularly when en-countering challenging scenarios like reverse loops. To address these limitations, we propose a loop closing network named LC-Net, which is designed to perform both place recognition and loop poses estimation tasks. Within the framework of the proposed method, the feature of keypoints is extracted and fed separately into the VLAD module and the RANSAC module to accomplish respective tasks. The evaluation indicates that the proposed method achieves high efficiency and outperforms some existing approaches. Additionally, we incorporate the proposed method into the LiDAR SLAM system, effectively enhancing trajectory accuracy.

articleTitle: MSRDN: A Super-Resolution Network for Human Body
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Innovations and Development of Information Technologies and Robotics (IDITR)
abstract: Recent advances in human parsing estimation implicitly assume the input image is of sufficiently high resolution (HR). However, person images are everywhere especially in the surveillance applications. This paper aims at super resolving a person image with different resolution. First of all, a multi-scale residual dense block (MSRDB) is proposed to completely gather sufficient features for human body image super resolution (SR) task. And then, a multi-scale residual dense network (MSRDN) is developed, which consists of a cascaded MSRDBs, to reconstruct HR outputs in a way that goes from coarse to fine. Experiments on human body benchmark datasets show that our method performs better than other SOTA methods in terms of PSNR and SSIM metrics. Further, body landmark estimation task is introduced as novel evaluation metrics for human body. Performance on the task further proves the effectiveness of our method.

articleTitle: Distributed Adaptive Test Monitoring Data Classification Technique Based on Data Fields
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Innovations and Development of Information Technologies and Robotics (IDITR)
abstract: Aiming at the problem that monitoring data in cross-domain tests face a large amount of data and cross categories, we establish a test monitoring data classification system, study the distributed adaptive data classification technology based on data fields, cut and assign the classification task to nodes at different levels by using a distributed data processing scheme to make the classification modular and low-coupling, and realize fast and accurate classification of cross-domain test monitoring data to achieve the purpose of improving the monitoring efficiency of test data by different test personnel and fast access to key data.

articleTitle: Research on GNSS/INS Integrated Navigation Positioning Method
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Innovations and Development of Information Technologies and Robotics (IDITR)
abstract: The high-precision positioning technology of intelligent vehicles mainly relies on GNSS/INS integrated navigation positioning technology, and on this basis, Kalman filtering is applied to process navigation data,Due to the limitations of traditional EKF, this article proposes the ST-EKF satellite integrated navigation technology and establishes corresponding mathematical models through algorithmic calculations. These models are used for prediction and measurement updates, and experimental data is obtained for comparison. The accuracy of ST-EKF satellite integrated navigation positioning is significantly better than that of traditional EKF satellite integrated.

articleTitle: Fault Prediction Method for SINS/GNSS Integrated Navigation System Based on SD-RBF Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Innovations and Development of Information Technologies and Robotics (IDITR)
abstract: In response to the problem of difficult prediction of slowly changing faults in Strapdown Intertial Navigation System / Global Navigation Satellite System(SINS/GNSS) integrated navigation system, this paper proposes a sliding window based double-layer Radial Basis Function(SD-RBF) fault prediction model when the system model and data distribution characteristics are difficult to obtain. This algorithm combines the explanatory model with the RBF based time series model. It uses system residuals to establish a time series prediction model and extracts fault trend information through residual analysis, achieving the prediction of slowly changing faults in SINS/GNSS integrated navigation. The simulation results show that the algorithm can predict slowly changing faults in 3 seconds, and the accuracy can reach 88%.

articleTitle: A Novelty of Face Recognition using Hybrid Artificial Intelligence Method
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Innovations and Development of Information Technologies and Robotics (IDITR)
abstract: In the context of the COVID-19 pandemic that occurred in the past year, people have had to adjust their daily lives to minimize physical contact, including the shift towards online learning, as traditional classroom settings became impractical. Educational institutions have heavily relied on online learning platforms, leading to challenges in measuring and maintaining students' engagement and attendance. Consequently, there has been a surge in research on facial recognition technology to aid in monitoring attendance and participation in online education. However, existing facial recognition systems often face limitations, particularly in terms of excessive data usage for training. The objective of this study is to enhance the efficiency of existing facial recognition systems and reduce resource consumption. In this research, we employed feature extraction techniques in conjunction with GoogLeNet Convolutional Neural Networks and Support Vector Machine, specifically focusing on extracting crucial facial features that remain consistent for training. The achieved facial recognition accuracy in this study reached up to 93%.

articleTitle: Research on Attitude Control of Launch Vehicle at Ascent Stage Through Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Innovations and Development of Information Technologies and Robotics (IDITR)
abstract: Focusing on the problem that existing control methods of launch vehicle have insufficient adaptability to the uncertainty in actual flight, an attitude control method of launch vehicle at ascent stage through reinforcement learning (RL) is proposed in this paper. Firstly, a public recorded launch vehicle named Ares-I is taken as the research object, and its dynamic model is built in the specific reference frame. Then, an RL framework based on Soft Actor Critic (SAC) algorithm is constructed for attitude control of Ares-I and a reward function considering the tracking error, trajectory stability and training speed is designed. Finally, through offline training, an RL based attitude controller of Ares-I is proposed. The simulations show that this method improves the control accuracy by an order of magnitude compared with the traditional PID controller.

articleTitle: Research on Part Feature Rule Description and Matching Algorithm based on Topological Relation
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Innovations and Development of Information Technologies and Robotics (IDITR)
abstract: The recognition and extraction of part processing features is an preliminary step for intelligent manufacturing, and can significantly facilitate the machining process design and resource allocation. This paper uses SolidWorks software, which is commonly used in the production process, to carry out secondary development. The feature description rules and matching algorithms are designed in common parts based on multi-attribute adjacency graph (MAAG), which ensure the rapidity and accuracy of feature recognition in the manufacturing process. The results of feature recognition in common parts store topological relationships between features, which is beneficial for the determination of co-planar features, co-processing direction features.

articleTitle: Research on Communication Security Strategy for Intelligent Connected Vehicles Based on HSM
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Innovations and Development of Information Technologies and Robotics (IDITR)
abstract: The development of intelligent connected vehicles cannot be separated from secure network communication. So far, a large number of security communication technologies have emerged, such as secure transport layer protocol, national secret TLS, etc. However, the number of vehicle attack events has not decreased but has become more frequent. One of the reasons is that the current mainstream in vehicle network CAN protocol lacks necessary security protection measures, and related communication security technologies still lack practical application in vehicle production. This article discusses the security strategy of intelligent connected vehicle communication based on HSM, including the establishment of an encryption channel using TLS with a national security dual certificate mechanism, secure key storage, signature, and signature verification and authentication mechanisms. Vehicle networking communication mainly includes external communication, security gateway, and in vehicle ECU communication. Both Android apps with Key Master functionality and Windows apps with TPM functionality can securely communicate with vehicles. With the help of certificates, certificate chains, ECDHE, and OpenSSL Engine mechanisms, secure communication between cloud, external devices, and vehicles can be achieved. This solution has been deployed and implemented in a certain automotive company.

articleTitle: Automatic Extraction of Operator Industry Specification Terms Based on Multi-Combination Unsupervised Methods
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Innovations and Development of Information Technologies and Robotics (IDITR)
abstract: The operator domain terminology extraction algorithm can extract the core vocabulary terms of the operator industry to understand the content of the operator's vertical scenarios quickly. Traditional supervised machine learning, sequence annotation methods require a large number of manual annotations, especially for domain-specific data, the annotators also need to have specialized knowledge and the cost is high. To address the above problems, this paper proposes to use a blend of unsupervised extraction methods for the automatic construction of the operator industry thesaurus by combining the statistical method TF-IDF and large model-based prompt extraction and other methods to obtain the operator industry terminology unigram, bigram and trigram, respectively, a total of 16,539 words, the accuracy of unigram automatic extraction reaches more than 95%, which can be used for operator industry knowledge search, Q&A and other fields.

articleTitle: A Sim-to-Real Pipeline for Stroke-Based Robotic Painting
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Innovations and Development of Information Technologies and Robotics (IDITR)
abstract: Representing art using a robotic system is part of artificial intelligence in our life, especially in the realm of emotional expression. Developing a painting robot involves addressing how to enable the robot to emulate human artistic processes, which often include imprecise techniques or errors akin to those made by human artists. This paper discusses our development of an innovative painting robot utilizing the sim-to-real approach within learning technology. Specifically, this pipeline operates under a deep reinforcement learning (DRL) framework designed to learn drawing strategies from training data derived from real-world settings, aiming for the robot's proficiency in emulating human artistic expressions. Accordingly, the framework comprises two modules when given a target drawing image: the first module trains in a simulated environment to break down the target image into individual strokes; the second module then learns how to execute these strokes in a real environment. Our experiments have shown that this system can meet our objectives effectively.

articleTitle: Reliability Analysis for Dependent Competing Failure System Considering Degradation Rate and Hard Failure Threshold Changes
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Innovations and Development of Information Technologies and Robotics (IDITR)
abstract: The failure of many systems often results from competing soft and hard failures, as they experience performance degradation and simultaneous multiple random shocks resulted from the changeable operating environment. On account of the assumption that the performance degradation process follows a linear degradation path model and the shock process follows an extreme shock model, the effects of multiple random shocks on the system performance degradation level, degradation rate, and the hard failure threshold are analyzed. Thereby, under the multiple random shocks, this study propose an innovative reliability model for dependent competing failure systems, which considers that the hard failure threshold will change as well as the degradation rate. Multiple random shocks accelerate the degradation process, causing abrupt increases in performance degradation levels and a rapid acceleration in the degradation rate. Furthermore, in the extreme shock model, previous shocks will cause a decrease of hard failure threshold. Based on the system description and the model assumptions, the expression of system reliability model is established through analysis and deduction, and the calculation is performed through Monte Carlo method. Ultimately, by the numerical experiments of Micro-engine mechanical system and sensitivity analysis of the model's basic parameters, it's proved that the proposed model is effective and accurate.

articleTitle: Trajectory optimization for spray-painting robot in Cartesian space based on consistency index of paint film thickness
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Innovations and Development of Information Technologies and Robotics (IDITR)
abstract: In response to the issue of uneven paint film thickness in Z-shaped spray trajectories during camouflage coating operations, this paper presents a robot spray trajectory optimization method based on a consistency evaluation index of the paint film thickness. Firstly, for the Z-shaped spray trajectory of the robot spray gun, a linear trajectory with seventh-degree polynomial blends is used to generate multi-point spray trajectories within the camouflage color blocks. Then, based on the paint deposition model of the rectangular gun, a consistency evaluation index for the paint film thickness is established. Finally, with the minimization of the variance in paint thickness as the optimization objective, the optimal spray trajectory is generated based on a genetic algorithm, with the interpolation time interval as the decision variable. Simulation and experiment results validate the effectiveness of the proposed method, demonstrating its capability to achieve a relatively uniform paint thickness while realizing a Z-shaped spray trajectory planning for camouflage blocks in Cartesian space.

articleTitle: Research on the surface topography inspection of sandpaper based on machine vision
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Innovations and Development of Information Technologies and Robotics (IDITR)
abstract: To solve the problems of low efficiency and high subjectivity of existing sandpaper morphology parameter detection methods, machine vision methods are used to detect the surface morphology characteristics of sandpaper. A weighted decision matrix is established to select the important parameters that can reflect the topography of the sandpaper surface; Zeiss Smartproof5 fast turntable confocal microscope equipment is used to obtain the true-color view of different sandpaper samples, the pseudo-color view based on the height, and the XYZ three-dimensional point cloud of the sandpaper surface; the image is preprocessed by the methods of threshold segmentation and morphology processing, and then segmented by watershed segmentation; and the key topographic parameters of different sandpaper samples are calculated and compared. The key morphological parameters of different sandpaper samples were calculated and compared. The results show that the number of abrasive grains, abrasive grain size and other parameters increase with the increase of mesh size, while the uniformity of sandpaper distribution decreases with the increase of mesh size. The results of this study can provide a theoretical reference for the realization of automated inspection of sandpaper surface topography.

articleTitle: Interpretable ML Model for Quality Control of Locks Using Counterfactual Explanations
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Innovations and Development of Information Technologies and Robotics (IDITR)
abstract: This paper presents an interpretable machine-learning model for anomaly detection in door locks using torque data. The model aims to replace the human tactile sense in the quality control process, reducing repetitive tasks and improving reliability. The model achieved an accuracy of 96%, however, to gain social acceptance and operators' trust, interpretability of the model is crucial. The purpose of this study was to evaluate an approach that can improve interpretability of anomalous classifications obtained from an anomaly detection model. We evaluate four instance-based counterfactual explanators, three of which, employ optimization techniques and one uses, a less complex, weighted nearest neighbor approach, which serve as our baseline. The former approaches, leverage a latent representation of the data, using a weighted principal component analysis, improving plausibility of the counter factual explanations and reduces computational cost. The explanations are presented together with the 5-50-95<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> percentile range of the training data, acting as a frame of reference to improve interpretability. All approaches successfully presented valid and plausible counterfactual explanations. However, instance-based approaches employing optimization techniques yielded explanations with greater similarity to the observations and was therefore concluded to be preferable despite the higher execution times (4-16s) compared to the baseline approach (0.1s). The findings of this study hold significant value for the lock industry and can potentially be extended to other industrial settings using timeseries data, serving as a valuable point of departure for further research.

articleTitle: Leveraging Computer Vision in AI for Efficient Image Analysis in Case Investigations
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Innovations and Development of Information Technologies and Robotics (IDITR)
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach using computer vision algorithms for image analysis facilitating regulators” investigation. Digital evidence is rapidly increasing, originating from selected data viewed through forensic tools. While conventional tools use keywords and metadata search, they fall short of the expectation when it comes to multimedia images on phones. Visual inspection is still relied upon for image selection. Manual selection becomes limited in complex cases with increasing image volumes. The proposed method addresses these challenges through Object Detection, Face Detection, and Optical Character Recognition (OCR). Object Detection classifies evidence, Face Detection identifies associates and OCR extracts text for keyword search and personal information identification. This i2i (images to insights) method enables fast and relevant image selection, aiding prosecution and ensuring search scope adherence. It also assists in redaction and handling privileged claims in its extended use.

articleTitle: Automatic Detection of Building Surface Structure Damage Based on Multi-UAV Collaboration
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Innovations and Development of Information Technologies and Robotics (IDITR)
abstract: The health condition of a building is related to the safety of people's lives and properties, so it is especially important to accurately detect its surface structure damage. Initial assessment of a building's health condition often involves identifying these cracks on its surface images. However, capturing these images traditionally relies on human labor, and the small pixel size of cracks in two-dimensional images makes segmentation challenging. In this study, a pioneering approach is introduced for automatic detection of building surface structure damage based on multi-UAV collaboration. The method comprises two primary components. Firstly, we introduce a reconstruction mathematical model based on MVS reconstruction rules to estimate the reconstruction quality. This model guides the extension of multi-UAV trajectories, considering trajectory energy consumption and security, enabling automated image capture and the creation of high-quality 3D models. Secondly, we design a spatial attention mechanism that incorporates Canny edge detection information and improve the deeplabV3 model to realize the automatic recognition of small cracks on building surfaces. Real-world experiments demonstrate that our method facilitates collaborative multi-UAV image capture, supporting high-quality 3D reconstruction and achieving precise crack segmentation.

articleTitle: TKG-SLAM: Dynamic SLAM based on target tracking and multi-view geometry
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Innovations and Development of Information Technologies and Robotics (IDITR)
abstract: The dynamic nature of the scene violates the static environment assumption of the SLAM algorithm, reducing the accuracy of camera positioning. In recent years, many studies have attempted to address dynamic objects by combining semantic constraints and geometric constraints, but issues like bad realtime performance, the potential to mistakenly treat people as static objects, and poor performance in highly dynamic environments still persist. Based on object detection, Kalman filtering and multi-view geometry, this paper proposes a dynamic scene visual SLAM algorithm called Dynamic SLAM based on target tracking and multi-view geometry (TKG-SLAM). This algorithm takes into consideration both realtime performance and algorithm accuracy. It combines semantic constraints and multi-view geometry constraints, selectively running the algorithm in different scenarios, filtering and preserving static points for camera pose estimation. Experimental results demonstrate that, compared to current state-of-the-art methods, our method performs optimally in some scenarios and has stronger realtime capabilities.
